title: Joint Root-N Limits for Dynamic Treatment Paths in Synthetic Blips
banked_reason: The load-bearing p_N>=ell_N N^(2+delta_0) condition has no concrete feasible design, the named Korean application lacks the proxies, and the stored proof architecture leaves validity at or below N^2 open.
gap_reasons: The load-bearing p_N>=ell_N N^(2+delta_0) condition is an instrumental proxy-volume strengthening; its justification gives no concrete data-generating design plausibly supplying superquadratically many suitably mixing proxy rows, and the named Korean application explicitly lacks them.

Replace the proxy-growth justification with a named feasible measurement design and a quantitative proxy-count audit, or weaken the headline to a slower-rate theorem under p comparable to N and retain the frontier as the principal open question.
proof_attempt_summary: The proposal repaired its LTV causal identification, donor recursion, uniform class, source-model alignment, and Gram assumptions while preserving a novel joint influence and donor-reuse covariance kernel. The feasible root-N expansion nevertheless continued to require superquadratically many proxy rows; under p comparable to N, its stored remainder envelope does not vanish, and the named Korean application has no such measurements. A future topic would need a new feasible nuisance-rate theorem or a different fixed-weight projection estimand, followed by a fresh novelty review.
tldr: For a fixed target unit and a finite menu of dynamic treatment paths, the causal model is a one-lag LTV potential-outcome system whose blips depend on treatment time, lag, action, and realized history. A donor-invariant backward graph maps every path to its counterfactual baseline and blip components. Over an explicit common-constant triangular-array class with geometrically mixing, high-effective-rank proxy rows and the narrow sufficient regime \(p_N\ge\ell_NN^{2+\delta_0}\), the focal result is a uniform joint root-\(N\) influence expansion for the entire causal path vector. A leave-one-unit-out replay of the full graph consistently estimates all donor-reuse covariance terms. Gaussian bands, maximizing-path sets, and local regret are downstream consequences; the weaker proxy-information frontier remains open.
gap: Synthetic Blips identifies history-dependent dynamic path means and proves pointwise SBE-PCR consistency, but it does not derive a joint source recursion, a root-(N) path-vector law, or covariance terms created when the same donor innovation is reused across nodes.
fill: The project maps potential-outcome blips to graph nodes, closes the algebra with donor-invariant propagation coefficients, proves orthogonal nuisance products negligible uniformly over the explicit class, and estimates the resulting full covariance by recursive residual replay.
